target_customer: Ambulatory surgery centers and hospitals performing abdominal and laparoscopic surgery that cannot afford large surgical robots
problem: Existing surgical robots are expensive and bulky; Revolve built a table-mounted, non-teleoperated system with 5mm wristed instruments for any operating room.
business_model: Capital equipment sale with instruments and software

founders.name: Peter Francis
prior_employers: Medical robotics startup in the Bay Area (Engineer #2, unnamed)
education: Undergraduate mechatronics engineering and graduate surgical robotics (schools not named)
founders.background_notes: From YC page bio; also worked on a CSA lunar rover.

founders.name: Matthew Kang
founders.background_notes: YC bio: builds MedTech, ML and computer vision, robots.

founders.name: Alex Gordon
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder by Innovation Factory and StartupIntros listings and as COO in a YC page search summary; not on the fetched YC page.

competitors.name: Intuitive Surgical da Vinci
competitors.what: Market leading teleoperated surgical robot; later pursued ambulatory surgery centers with refurbished lower cost systems

technical_complexity.rationale: Surgical robot with wristed 5mm instruments, table mounting and clinical safety requirements, with FDA clearance needed before sale.

defensibility.rationale: FDA 510(k) clearance, patents and mechanical design make copying slow, though larger rivals have more resources.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition reported; incumbents moved toward lower cost offerings for ASCs by 2025 and 2026.

market_need_then: The company said over a million abdominal surgeries a year in the US occur outside hospitals, per its YC description, and large robots were priced for hospitals.

identity.visual_style: Clinical and minimal, product imagery of table-mounted arm
identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical, mission driven (raise the baseline in every operating room)

brand_strength.rationale: A clean name but only trade press coverage of the FDA clearance in March 2026; no community or brand driven growth evidence.

outcome_analysis: Revolve Surgical is a Toronto surgical robotics company from the Summer 2021 batch that stayed small and low funded in public data yet reached FDA 510(k) clearance for its table-mounted robot in March 2026, with the first appendectomy using the arm reported that month. Its path shows a capital efficient, regulation gated route; commercial launch awaits broader laparoscopic clearance and funding is not publicly itemized.
notes: Funding: aggregators list a pre-seed of about $125K to $130K around August 2021 (Seedtable, TipRanks, CB Insights) and an incubator entry in January 2026; since these come only from aggregators they are not recorded as rounds. No press release for any round was found. The MassDevice article returned 403; clearance date is from the MassRobotics and Becker's summaries. Competitor source is from 2026; no 2021 dated competitor source found for low cost ASC surgical robots (Titan Medical did not appear). Founder education schools not named. Brand name origin not found.
